Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Pathum Nissanka and Kamil Mishara are the two openers for Sri Lanka. Luke Wood has the new ball in hand. Let's go...
…THE RUN CHASE…

Chameera shines as Sri Lanka dominate England - Sri Lanka’s bowlers were relentless, maintaining pressure throughout England’s innings. Dushmantha Chameera stole the spotlight with a five-wicket haul, while Pathirana, Theekshana, and Wellalage delivered tight spells to keep their team firmly in control. Now chasing a modest target of 129, Sri Lanka will be confident of sealing the victory and ending the series on a high. Will they cruise to the win, or will England fight back with the ball? We’ll find out soon. Stay tuned for the second innings.

A struggling batting display for England - England put in a below-par batting effort, finishing with a modest total of 128/9 from their 20 overs. Opting to bat first, the visitors found themselves in early trouble, losing four wickets for just 34 runs inside the Powerplay. Things worsened when Buttler and Jacks were dismissed, leaving England reeling at 60/6. A 47-run partnership between Sam Curran and Liam Dawson brought some stability, but wickets continued to fall at crucial moments, preventing the side from posting a competitive score. Curran was the standout performer with 58 off 48 balls, while the rest of the batting lineup struggled. Ultimately, England had to settle for a total below 130.

Pitch Report - Nick Compton is at pitchside and describes the surface as dry and hard, noting it’s the third match played here. He mentions that while the series is already decided, this game remains important for both teams as they focus on the upcoming World Cup. Compton highlights that Sri Lanka’s batting has struggled in the middle overs, with an average under 20 and a strike rate around 123. He credits Adil Rashid for this, praising his pace, turn, and bounce. On England’s side, Compton says they’ve done what was needed but may experiment with their combination. He adds that they’ll look to improve their opening overs, as they haven’t taken many wickets with the new ball so far.

The captain of Sri Lanka - Dasun Shanaka, says that they would have bowled first. Adds that the conditions seem to get better with the dew in the second innings. Says that they could have done better in the second game. Mentions that Wanindu Hasaranga and Eshan Malinga are injured, and Charith Asalanka has been rested.

The captain of England - Harry Brook, wins the toss and opts to bat first. Adds that it's a used pitch and they will get the best of it in the first innings. Mentions the changes in their side. Adds that they will keep backing their changes and play their natural game. He closes by saying that it is nice to be in Sri Lanka.

Final chance for Sri Lanka - Now, with one final chance to respond, Sri Lanka will be hoping for a spirited performance to restore some pride before the global showpiece. Can England complete a 3–0 whitewash, or will Sri Lanka roar back in style to end the series on a high? Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned.

England aim to test bench strength - England head into this contest on the back of a six-wicket win (DLS method) in the second T20I. Chasing 168 in a rain-curtailed 17-over match, Tom Banton starred with a brisk half-century, supported by quickfire cameos from Jos Buttler and Harry Brook to seal the chase with a couple of balls to spare. Earlier, the spin trio of Adil Rashid, Will Jacks, and Liam Dawson put in impressive performances to restrict Sri Lanka to a manageable total. With the series already secured, England may look to rotate their squad and give valuable game time to a few fringe players ahead of the upcoming mega event.

Sri Lanka’s batting shows promise - Sri Lanka, meanwhile, showed promise with the bat in the second game, posting a strong total of 189 thanks to contributions across the lineup, with Pavan Rathnayake top-scoring with 40. However, despite their bowlers taking the contest deep, they were unable to contain England at the death. Pathirana, Shanaka, and Wellalage picked up wickets, but costly runs in the final overs allowed the visitors to cross the line and clinch the series.

England eye clean sweep - Hello and welcome to our coverage of the third and final T20I of the three-match series between Sri Lanka and England, from the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy. Having wrapped up the series with victories in the first two matches, England will be eyeing a clean sweep, while Sri Lanka will be desperate to salvage some pride and finish the series on a positive note.
…MATCHDAY…

Match intro - The stage is set for a thrilling finale at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium. While England has already secured the series with a 2-0 lead, the third T20I is far from a dead rubber. With the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026 kicking off in just a few days, this match serves as the ultimate dress rehearsal for both nations. Dominant England - England has looked clinical in sub-continental conditions, adapting their ultra-aggressive style to the slower, spin-friendly tracks of Kandy. Taking over the reins, Harry Brook has impressed not just with his tactical bowling changes but with his lead-from-the-front batting. His cameo in the second T20I, striking at 300, effectively broke the back of the Sri Lankan spin threat. This final match is his last chance to fine-tune his leadership before the World Cup. Sri Lanka's search for consistency - The hosts have shown flashes of brilliance in both departments but have struggled to sustain pressure. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis have provided brisk starts, but the middle order has been prone to collapses. On the bowling front, expect the Lankans to lean heavily on Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana to exploit any complacency in the England camp. Spin vs Power - The battle between England's power-hitters, including the likes of Phil Salt and Jos Buttler, and Sri Lanka’s spin-heavy attack will define the Powerplay. On the flip side, England's veteran spinner Adil Rashid has been the silent assassin of the series, consistently stifling the Lankan run rate in the middle overs. Pallekele has lived up to its reputation as a high-scoring ground with something for the spinners. However, rain has been a persistent visitor during this series. The forecast for Tuesday suggests scattered showers, so the DLS calculation and the toss will likely play a massive role once again. Is 0-3 loading for Sri Lanka? The last time Sri Lanka were clean-swept in a bilateral T20I series of 3 or more matches at home was against South Africa in 2021. It is a very rare occurrence for the Lankans to lose at home and that too so heavily. Given the timing and a home T20 World Cup on the horizon, it will be a big blow to the team's morale. On the other end, you wouldn't put it past England to achieve a clean sweep as they look like a side that's hungry for more, which hasn't been the case in recent times, at least not in white-ball cricket. Form (Last 5 completed T20Is, most recent first) - Sri Lanka - LLWLL | England - WWWWW. Which way will the pendulum swing? While Sri Lanka will be desperate to avoid a 3-0 whitewash on home soil, England’s depth and recent form make them heavy favorites. England’s ability to find boundaries even against elite spin gives them the edge. We can expect a tight contest as both teams look to put their best foot forward heading into the mega event.
